summary:
William Clyde “Bill” Elliott (born 1955), known as “Awesome Bill from Dawsonville,” is a former NASCAR driver with 44 Winston Cup wins and the 1988 championship. His victories included two Daytona 500s, three Southern 500s and the 2002 Brickyard 400. In 1985, he won the Daytona 500, Winston 500 and Southern 500 to earn NASCAR’s first Winston Million bonus, and finished second in the season standings.

Elliott set qualifying records at Daytona and Talladega in 1987. His Talladega speed of 212.809 mph remains the fastest qualifying speed in NASCAR history; restrictor plates introduced at both tracks in 1988 make the records unlikely to be broken. He won NASCAR’s Most Popular Driver Award 16 times, withdrawing from the ballot after his 2002 win. Named one of NASCAR’s 50 Greatest Drivers in 1998, he entered the Hall of Fame in 2015. His son Chase won the 2020 Cup championship. Bill Elliott last competed part-time in SRX in 2022.
